chunk_findings.detail: The new `_charged_line` call is outside the `if out.kind != "ok"` branch that records the `asked[1:]` gates as `unavailable`, so it also runs when a combined review cannot run. In that failure path no full round is charged; the only records are `unavailable`, and `_rounds_used(...)` still reports the prior count (e.g. `0/4`). The output then falsely says `combined review charged one full round to each gate: rounds used now rubber_duck 0/4, critic 0/4`. A failing combined review such as the first gate returning non-ok therefore misreports that a round was spent, defeating the round-tracking fix.

chunk_findings.detail: For `--probe tests/test_real.py::TestB::test_no_such_thing_at_all`, the new regression test expects the whole node id in the refusal. But this change only appends `(looked in ...)` to the existing `', '.join(missing)` interpolation; it never changes how `missing` is produced. Since the reported bug is that `_unresolved_tests` returns/prints only the truncated name, this line still returns `probe names test_no_such_thing_at_all, which no worktree defines (looked in ...)` and the new test assertion fails. The change does not fix B-triage-error-truncates-test-name.

chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal sentence says a probe “must name an existing test as a path::node id ... or a command that was run”, but `probe_problem` still accepts a bare defined test name: when `_BARE_TEST` matches a bare name and `_defined_anywhere` finds it, the loop falls through and returns `""`. So in a project where `tests/test_real.py` defines `test_real`, `--probe covered by test_real` is accepted, yet the refusal message for other probes tells the author that only `path::node id`/command forms are accepted. That is a false description of the accepted inputs.

chunk_findings.detail: The change does not fix the stated truncation bug. The missing branch still interpolates `', '.join(missing)` exactly as before; no line in this diff changes how `missing` is computed. For `--probe tests/test_real.py::test_not_there`, the unchanged `_unresolved_tests` behavior would still put only the truncated leaf name in `missing`, so line 294 still returns something like `probe names test_not_there, which no worktree defines (looked in tests/ of every worktree)`. The newly added regression test asserts only `"tests/ of every worktree"`; it never asserts the full node id `tests/test_real.py::test_not_there`, so it passes even when the truncation remains. The actual bug is therefore still unverified and unfixed.

chunk_findings.detail: The change claims to fix B-triage-error-truncates-test-name by printing the full node id, but the part of the message that produced the truncated name is left unchanged. The old return already interpolated `', '.join(missing)`, and the new return still interpolates the same unchanged `missing` list from the unchanged `_unresolved_tests(roots[-1], ...)` call; the manifest contains no change to `_unresolved_tests`. For the reported input `tests/x.py::name` where `_unresolved_tests` returns only `name`, this code still returns `probe names name, ...` and never prints `tests/x.py::name`. The added regression test `test_a_missing_node_names_the_whole_id_and_the_accepted_forms` asserts that full id is present, so it should still fail on this implementation unless `_unresolved_tests` was already returning the full id, which would mean the change under review is not the fix.
